components.css: :host{--ember-400:#ff6a3d;--ember-500:#f04e1f;--ember-600:#cf3c12;--clay-50:#f2f1ee;--clay-100:#e7e5e1;--clay-300:#aeaaa3;--clay-400:#85817a;--clay-500:#625e58;--clay-700:#2f2d2b;--clay-800:#1d1c1b;--clay-900:#131312;--clay-950:#0b0b0b;} .ds-card{font-family:'Readex Pro',system-ui,sans-serif;display:block;padding:24px;border-radius:3px;background:var(--clay-900);color:var(--clay-100);border:1px solid var(--clay-800);text-decoration:none;transition:border-color .3s,box-shadow .3s}.ds-card h3{margin:0 0 8px;font-size:20px;font-weight:600;color:var(--clay-50)}.ds-card p{margin:0;font-size:14px;color:var(--clay-400)}.ds-card:hover{border-color:rgba(240,78,31,.7);box-shadow:0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.04) inset,0 24px 48px -24px rgba(0,0,0,.7)}.ds-card:focus-visible{outline:1.5px solid var(--ember-500);outline-offset:3px}

components.css: :host{--ember-400:#ff6a3d;--ember-500:#f04e1f;--ember-600:#cf3c12;--clay-50:#f2f1ee;--clay-100:#e7e5e1;--clay-300:#aeaaa3;--clay-400:#85817a;--clay-500:#625e58;--clay-700:#2f2d2b;--clay-800:#1d1c1b;--clay-900:#131312;--clay-950:#0b0b0b;} .ds-nav{font-family:'Readex Pro',system-ui,sans-serif;display:flex;gap:28px;padding:12px 16px;background:rgba(11,11,11,.85);border-bottom:1px solid var(--clay-800)}.ds-nav a{position:relative;padding:8px 0;font-size:15px;font-weight:500;color:#d1cec8;text-decoration:none;transition:color .2s}.ds-nav a:hover,.ds-nav a.is-active{color:var(--clay-50)}.ds-nav a::after{content:'';position:absolute;inset-inline:0;bottom:-4px;height:6px;background:#45423e;-webkit-mask:url('/textures/brush-stroke.svg') center/100% 100% no-repeat;mask:url('/textures/brush-stroke.svg') center/100% 100% no-repeat;transform:scaleX(0);transform-origin:left;transition:transform .3s ease-out}.ds-nav a:hover::after{transform:scaleX(1);opacity:.6}.ds-nav a.is-active::after{transform:scaleX(1);opacity:1}.ds-nav a:focus-visible{outline:1.5px solid var(--ember-500);outline-offset:3px}

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "Each Edition Is Fired Once"**

The site is a raku kiln. A carbon ground with fine soot grain holds crackled-glaze panels and hairline kiln frames; the only heat in the room is ember, the festival's raku flash colour, and it is spent exclusively on what is live right now. The current edition's name is brushed huge in Lalezar and arrives ember-hot, then cools into crackled glaze; past editions sit in the archive already cooled, as soot numerals and glazed tiles. Body copy is austere Readex Pro so Arabic reads comfortably beneath the loud brushed display.

Dark (carbon) is the default ground, applied before first paint; light (ash) is the alternate. Arabic RTL is the primary reading direction and every rule is written RTL-first. One codebase builds three festivals: the layout, textures and rules never change, only the clay tint and the ember hue are swapped at build time via `FESTIVAL`.

The world refuses the red-curtain-and-gold theatre site: no velvet, no gilt, no spotlights.
keyCharacteristics: Carbon/ash ground with a fixed soot-grain overlay (5% light, 9% dark).
Crackled-glaze raster surfaces (`/textures/glaze-*.webp`, procedurally authored, provenance sidecars beside each).
Ember is scarce and semantic: live = ember, upcoming = glaze, past = soot.
Brushed display type (SVG `#brush` displacement filter) over clean sans body.
Dry-brush stroke swipes under headings: ember when live, cooled clay otherwise.

rules.name: The Live Heat Rule
rules.body: Ember fills (backgrounds, glowing dots, ember swipes, fire animation) are reserved for what is live now: the current edition's live action, today's show, a confirmed booking, the running stage. Everything else is clay, glaze or soot. If two unrelated things on one screen are ember-filled, one of them is not live.

rules.name: The Warm-On-Touch Rule
rules.body: Interactive hairlines may warm to ember on hover or focus (border, underline decoration, icon tint) as a response to the hand. That is heat borrowed for an instant, not a fill; at rest they are clay.

rules.name: The Three Kilns Rule
rules.body: Never hard-code a festival hex. Use the `ember-*` / `primary-*` scales (`secondary`, `accent` are ember aliases) so all three festivals rebuild correctly.

rules.name: The RTL Label Rule
rules.body: Tracking and uppercase are Latin devices. Under `dir=rtl` every label, badge and button drops letter-spacing and text-transform and steps up in size. Never track Arabic.

rules.name: The Tabular Ledger Rule
rules.body: Dates, times, counts and edition numbers use tabular lining numerals (`.tabular`).

rules.name: The Heat Not Height Rule
rules.body: Nothing scales or translates on hover. Interactive state is shown by colour, frame warmth and the glow under the surface.

dos: Do reserve ember fills for what is live now: current edition's live action, today's show, a confirmed booking, the running stage.
Do cool everything else to clay, glaze or soot; past posters go grayscale.
Do use 3px corners (2px for tags) and 1px hairline frames.
Do set page titles in brushed Lalezar with the crackle fill, followed by a brush swipe (ember only if live, `swipe-cool` otherwise).
Do use lucide icons at strokeWidth 1.25–1.75.
Do write RTL-first with logical properties, and leave Arabic labels untracked.
Do use the `ember-*` / `primary-*` scales so all three festivals rebuild.
Do honour reduced motion: fire, smoke and kiln animations collapse; the live title keeps its static ember residue.
donts: Don't use ember for decoration, section accents, or anything past or merely upcoming.
Don't scale or lift on hover; show state with colour, frame warmth and glow.
Don't put eyebrows or kickers above headings.
Don't use emoji as icons or logos; the kiln mark replaced them.
Don't reach for red curtains, gold, or spotlight imagery.
Don't round corners past 3px or add drop shadows to resting cards.
